defects: Moiré and shimmer in the fine wave guilloché at mid and far distance (frame 3, dial rim), where the pattern beats against the pixel grid
Dial print ('72 HEURES') falls fully out of focus in the first two shots, so it reads as a smudge rather than intended depth of field
The '72-hour power reserve' caption is a small, thin, default-looking sans laid flat over a busy pattern with no plate or contrast control
'Atelier Vauclair · 150 pièces' subline is tiny and low-contrast against the dark background and would not survive compression
End card is nearly static for about 2 s (change per second 4.6, then 0.8): a dead tail with no settle animation
Shot 1 and shot 2 are the same macro angle with only a light sweep, which reads as one shot held too long (longest shot 3.5 s)
Dial and case surfaces have a CG-clean, slightly plasticky specular, with little micro-surface roughness or dust
gaps: Choreography is slow camera drifts plus one light sweep per shot. There are no designed hand-offs, match cuts or mechanical motion such as hands, crown or rotor driving the edits. The pattern rippling across the dial is the only idea, and it is shown the same way in every shot, never built up.

The sound is a metronomic tick on a roughly 1 s grid, a sparse synth pad and a generic white-noise riser from 6.5 to 9.3 s that just stops. Cuts and type reveals don't land on the ticks, the peak has no designed impact or sub hit, and the tail decays into silence under a static end card.

Finish and type are below luxury-watch standard. The guilloché aliases at distance, there is no tasteful falloff on the dial print, and the type system (a display serif plus default sans captions) is placed by default rather than given an editorial layout, a reveal tied to the mechanism, or a closing composition that rhymes with the opening macro.
